source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

morphology.leaves: Opposite or upper alternate (genus); ovate to lanceolate, 3–15 cm long by ~20–70 mm wide; serrate, 3-nerved, aromatic, reduced above
morphology.heads: Small wind-pollinated heads, sessile in axils of linear to ovate bracts; 3–4 distinct phyllaries (key), involucre 4–5 mm broad
morphology.flowers: Peripheral pistillate and central staminate, 1.5–2.5 mm corollas; no pappus
morphology.habitat: Moist low ground, calcareous or sand; can form large stands

notes: Contrast historical Iva angustifolia by free versus united phyllaries and broader versus narrower leaves.

morphology.habit: Annual with branched, leafy stems; milky latex (genus)
morphology.leaves: Alternate, lower crowded, blades oblong or oblanceolate, entire/toothed/lobed
morphology.heads: Small yellow all-ligulate heads, phyllaries 4–10, prominently keeled in age (key)
morphology.pappus: Absent (species key), unlike reduced bristles/scales of K. wrightii
morphology.forms: forma cespitosa: heads 3–6 mm, flowering involucres 3–4.3 mm, corollas 2–4 mm; forma gracilis: heads 6–9 mm, involucres 5.3–8.3 mm, corollas 5–10 mm
morphology.habitat: Moist or disturbed sites, sandy or calcareous depending on historical form

notes: Forms intergrade and molecular data in 1999 flora did not separate them; avoid assigning from photographs without enough evidence.

morphology.habit: Scapose annual 4–16 cm tall, flower stems usually leafless and unbranched
morphology.heads: Yellow ligulate flower heads; 4–7 phyllaries; corollas 3.5–3.8 mm
morphology.pappus: Typically 5 short bristles 0.8–2 mm and 5 small scales

notes: Species distinct from leafy branched K. cespitosa; use both stem architecture and magnified pappus.

morphology.habit: Biennial 1–2 m, thick root crown, milky to brownish latex (1999 key favors brownish)
morphology.leaves: Alternate, pinnately lobed, upper increasingly triangular/clasping with prickly teeth; abaxial midrib sometimes prickly
morphology.heads: All ligulate, typically yellow corollas (rare blue reported but not locally confirmed)
morphology.fruit: Flattened somewhat winged cypselae 4.5–5 mm body, 7–10 mm including fine beak; 1–3 nerves per face, pappus bristles 7–10 mm

notes: Flora warns of possible intergradation with L. canadensis; fruit measurements more informative than leaves alone.

morphology.habit: Old-World introduced annual 0.5–2 m, taproot, white latex
morphology.leaves: Alternate, often pinnatifid, clasping above, spiny-toothed margins and prickles on underside midrib
morphology.heads: Narrow all-ligulate yellow heads; corollas dry bluish
morphology.fruit: Cypselae 2.5–3 mm body, ca. 1 mm wide with 5–7 nerves per face; beak filiform 3–4 mm; pappus fine white hairs

notes: Do not apply local-native status: regional flora explicitly identifies Old World origin.

records.printed_page: Liatris mucronata DC. (historical flora species concept; CURRENT NAME CROSSWALK NEEDS REVIEW)

morphology.habit: Perennial from swollen corm-like underground organ (genus); stems 0.3–0.8 m in flora's L. mucronata treatment
morphology.leaves: Alternate, narrow nearly sessile, often resin-dotted (genus)
morphology.heads: Crowded spike-like raceme 8–60 cm, 3–6 florets per head per key
morphology.involucres: Inner phyllaries generally <12 mm, closely packed along axis
morphology.pappus: Conspicuously plumose, 6–7 mm, side hairs ~15× bristle thickness or more in genus key

notes: IMPORTANT: crosswalk supplied by existing species.json, not independently nomenclaturally approved; source treatment should not overwrite L. punctata until taxonomic concept checked.

morphology.leaves: Alternate/subopposite or uppermost opposite, oblanceolate to rhombic-ovate-lanceolate, entire/coarsely toothed, sessile/short-petiolate
morphology.heads: Usually solitary or few in corymbs, peduncles 1–4 cm, involucres 10–15 mm high with two phyllary rows
morphology.phyllaries: Outer narrower, longer and more pointed than inner
morphology.rays: Usually five yellow/orange-yellow, pistillate fertile, 2-toothed ~10 mm ligules
morphology.fruit: Relatively large flattened ray cypselae almost as large as inner phyllaries, pappus two awns
morphology.habitat: Clayey prairie and roadsides, sometimes sandy

notes: Fruit sets on RAY florets unlike Helianthus where disk florets fruit; useful composite-head comparison.

morphology.habit: Low glabrous glaucous perennial from deep thick woody root; rhizomes increase with age, forming clumps; 20–65 cm
morphology.leaves: Mostly basal, linear/lanceolate, usually deeply pinnately lobed, upper stems largely reduced to bracts
morphology.stems: Openly and stiffly branched distally, milky latex
morphology.florets: All ligulate purple to lavender, rarely white, sweet-scented, open in morning

notes: Distinguish from radiate purple composites: every fertile floret is ligulate, not a distinct central disk.

morphology.habit: Small perennial, stems glabrous to finely pubescent above
morphology.leaves: Sessile or basal petiolate, oblanceolate to linear 5–15 cm × up to 1(–1.5) cm, entire
morphology.heads: Terminal 1–few heads 2.5–3.5 cm wide on long peduncles; no rays
morphology.phyllaries: Narrow green leafy bracts gradually transitioning into receptacle scales
morphology.flowers: Sweet-scented white or occasionally pinkish disk florets
morphology.pappus: Five scales 2–3(–4) mm, about as long as mature cypsela
morphology.varieties: var. caespitosa basal clustered leaves, heads typically solitary; var. signata stem leafy with heads solitary to several

notes: Do not infer variety from species-level video/photos.

morphology.habit: Herbaceous to weakly subshrubby perennial 15–50 cm
morphology.leaves: Opposite, linear to narrowly oblong 2–4.5 cm × up to 1 cm, sessile, entire to pinnately lobed
morphology.phyllaries: Outer series connate for more than half length, inner each surrounds a fertile ray cypsela and expands into a hood
morphology.discs: Yellow staminate florets with abortive ovaries

notes: Disk florets are functionally staminate; don't portray the yellow disk as primary seed source.

morphology.leaves: Opposite petiolate, ovate or deltate, often acuminate and nearly entire/wavy
morphology.heads: Corymbiform clusters of discoid heads with four equal pointed phyllaries, 4–5 mm
morphology.florets: Exactly four whitish sometimes pink-tinged disk florets per head; rays absent

notes: Flora notes this as only twining Asteraceae vine in its regional scope, not necessarily worldwide.

holds.name: Iva asperifolia var. angustifolia
holds.note: Existing repository synonym Iva angustifolia; historical flora p.378 treats I. angustifolia at species rank; verify accepted variety status and synonym concept before transfer.

holds.name: Hymenopappus scabiosaeus
holds.note: Prior extraction covers only var. corymbosus. Do not treat species-wide infraspecific traits as a new distinct taxon without source check.
